newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Q3 operating expenses mushroom 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: KLM Q3 operating expenses mushroom 12 pct.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Tuesday its third-quarter operating loss reflected a sharply higher wage bill, spiralling fuel costs and increased charges for landing, air navigation and third-party handling.
The Dutch flag carrier booked an operating loss of 19 million guilders in the third quarter, compared with a profit of 56 million guilders in the year-earlier period.
Analysts' estimates had ranged from an operating loss of 25 million guilders to a 35 million guilder profit.
KLM said third quarter operating expenses mushroomed by 268 million guilders or 12 percent to 2.57 billion.

"Most significant were the increases in salaries and benefits (up 11 percent), aircraft fuel (up 40 pct), landing and air navigation charges (up 12 pct) and third-party handling (up 15 percent)," KLM said in a results statement.

It said operational lease expenses had more than doubled to 48 million guilders in the third quarter from a year-earlier 23 million due to the introduction of five more Boeing 767 aircraft during the 1996/97 financial year.
Altogether unit costs rose by seven percent to 70.9 cents per available tonne-kilometre, it said.
